content:
In early 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Apple, accusing it of engaging in "smartphone monopoly" behaviour.

Over the past two years, Apple has publicly opposed the lawsuit on multiple occasions. According to Bloomberg, the Department of Justice and Apple are currently in settlement negotiations over the case.

Bloomberg noted that Apple has put forward "multiple proposals" this year in an attempt to reach a settlement with the Department of Justice:

The report also cautioned that although the negotiations are still ongoing, there is no guarantee that Apple and the Department of Justice will ultimately reach an agreement.

The Department of Justice's antitrust lawsuit against Apple mainly revolves around five aspects of the iPhone user experience: super apps, cloud streaming games, third-party messaging apps, third-party smartwatches and third-party digital wallets.

Over the past year, Apple has made significant changes in response to the Department of Justice's concerns, including adding RCS support to the Messages app, launching a brand-new "Mini App Partner Programme" on the App Store, and enhancing the openness of the iPhone NFC chip.

Whether these changes will satisfy the Department of Justice remains unknown. Admittedly, political factors are also involved, and Bloomberg has also mentioned this point:

Apple and the Department of Justice recently submitted a joint status report to the court to update the case progress. In addition, Apple won a case earlier this week in a dispute involving the disclosure of documents obtained from federal government agencies related to the Department of Justice case.

9to5Mac's view

If Apple and the Department of Justice ultimately reach a settlement, it would greatly ease the burden on John Ternus, who is scheduled to take over as Apple's CEO in September.
